name: cat
summary: Arrays joined along a dimension: 1 stacks them vertically, 2 side by side, 3 or more into new pages.
doc: The arrays' sizes must agree except along `dim`. `cat(1, ...)` is `[A; B]` and `cat(2, ...)` is `[A, B]`. Cell arrays join into a cell array, and char arrays into a char array.
differs: Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.

name: eye
signature:
I = eye(n)
I = eye(m, n)
I = eye(sz)
I = eye(___, typename)
I = eye(___, 'like', p)
summary: An identity matrix: ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere, square or m-by-n.
doc: Only two dimensions: `eye(2, 2, 2)` is an error, as in MATLAB. `typename` and `'like'` work as for `zeros`; `'like'` a sparse matrix gives a sparse identity.
differs: Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.

name: length
summary: The length of an array's largest dimension, or 0 for an empty array.
doc: `length(X)` is `max(size(X))` when X isn't empty, and 0 when it is.

name: linspace
signature:
y = linspace(x1, x2)
y = linspace(x1, x2, n)
summary: A row of n evenly spaced points from x1 to x2, both included; 100 points by default.
doc: The spacing is $(x_2 - x_1)/(n - 1)$ and the last point is x2 itself. `n` = 1 gives x2; `n` of 0 or less gives a 1-by-0 row; a non-integer `n` is rounded down. Complex and single endpoints work, the result being single when either endpoint is.
differs: Integer-class endpoints (linspace(int8(0), int8(10), 3)) are refused rather than given a guessed class.
Endpoints must be scalars: the vector form linspace([0 1], [1 2], n) is refused.
Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.

name: numel
summary: The number of elements of an array: the product of its dimensions.
doc: Counts every element, for numeric, logical and char arrays, cell arrays and struct arrays alike. A string scalar has one element.

name: ones
signature:
X = ones(n)
X = ones(sz1, ..., szN)
X = ones(sz)
X = ones(___, typename)
X = ones(___, 'like', p)
summary: An array of ones of a given size, double by default, or of a named class or the class, complexity and sparsity of a prototype.
doc: Takes the same size and class arguments as `zeros`.
differs: Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.

name: repmat
signature:
B = repmat(A, n)
B = repmat(A, r1, ..., rN)
B = repmat(A, r)
summary: An array repeated as tiles: n copies along each of the first two dimensions, or a given count along each dimension.
doc: Works for numeric, logical and char arrays, cell arrays and struct arrays.
differs: A count of 0 (repmat([1 2], 0, 1)) is an error, where MATLAB gives an empty array.

name: reshape
signature:
B = reshape(A, sz1, ..., szN)
B = reshape(A, sz)
summary: The elements of an array, in their column-major order, rearranged into new dimensions with the same number of elements.
doc: One size may be `[]`, computed from the others. The number of elements must not change. Works for numeric, logical and char arrays and cell arrays.
differs: Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.

name: size
signature:
sz = size(A)
szdim = size(A, dim)
szdim = size(A, dim1, ..., dimN)
szdim = size(A, vecdim)
[sz1, ..., szN] = size(___)
summary: The lengths of an array's dimensions, as a row vector, for chosen dimensions, or as separate outputs.
doc: With several outputs, the last one is the product of the remaining dimensions, and outputs past the array's dimensions are 1. A dimension past the array's is 1.
differs: Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.

name: zeros
signature:
X = zeros(n)
X = zeros(sz1, ..., szN)
X = zeros(sz)
X = zeros(___, typename)
X = zeros(___, 'like', p)
summary: An array of zeros of a given size, double by default, or of a named class or the class, complexity and sparsity of a prototype.
doc: `zeros(n)` is n-by-n; `zeros(m, n, ...)` and `zeros([m n ...])` give each dimension. A size of 0 or less gives an empty dimension; a size that isn't an integer is an error. `typename` is a numeric class name or `'logical'`; `'like', p` takes p's class, complexity and sparsity.
differs: Tables, timetables, datetime and duration arrays, and gpuArray or distributed arrays are not supported.
